source: Encoded from public post-mortems (The DAO, Cream, Euler, Nomad, Wormhole, Ronin, Poly Network, Curve Vyper, Mango, Cashio, Beanstalk, Inverse, Rari, Fei, Wintermute, KyberSwap Elastic, Bonq, Prisma, Penpie, Radiant, Cetus, Compound, Harvest, bZx) plus Immunefi 2025-2026 loss reports, Sherlock/C4 2024-2025 judging, OWASP SC Top 10 2026 and SWC. Recent incidents also live in incidents.json so they train retrieval without minting catalog detectors.

vectors.title: Classic reentrancy: external call before state settlement
vectors.description: A state-changing function performs an external call or ETH transfer before it finishes writing the balances, shares, or claimed flags that the call can observe.
vectors.exploit: An attacker contract re-enters the same or a sibling function during the callback and drains funds while the accounting still shows a pre-call balance.
vectors.remediation: Apply checks-effects-interactions, clear the claimable amount first, and add a reentrancy lock that covers every function sharing the mutated state.
vectors.proof_obligation: Trace every external call and prove all affected storage is finalized before control leaves the contract.

vectors.title: Read-only reentrancy against a view used as a price or share rate
vectors.description: A view function exposes transient pool or vault state during an external callback. Downstream protocols treat that view as a trustworthy price.
vectors.exploit: Trigger a liquidity removal that calls out, read the stale virtual price from a callback, and borrow or mint against the inflated valuation.
vectors.remediation: Lock view functions that feed oracles, or snapshot the rate before any external call and expose only the snapshot.
vectors.proof_obligation: Show no view consumed by another protocol can observe a mid-function reserve or share rate.

vectors.title: Spot AMM reserves used as a price oracle
vectors.description: Collateral, mint, or liquidation logic prices an asset from a single-block AMM spot or a raw token balance.
vectors.exploit: Flash-loan the pool, move the spot price, borrow or liquidate against the manipulated valuation, then restore the pool and repay the loan in one transaction.
vectors.remediation: Use a manipulation-resistant oracle (Chainlink, Uniswap v3 TWAP with sufficient window and liquidity, or a committee with freshness checks).
vectors.proof_obligation: Prove every pricing input has a window, liquidity floor, freshness bound, and cannot be moved profitably in one transaction.

vectors.title: Unauthenticated flash-loan or hook callback
vectors.description: A callback intended to be invoked only by a pool or lender does not bind initiator, asset, amount, and caller.
vectors.exploit: Call the callback directly with attacker-chosen amounts to mint, liquidate, or steal approvals without posting a real loan.
vectors.remediation: Require msg.sender to be the canonical pool, bind the initiator, and reconcile amount plus fee against the actual balance delta.
vectors.proof_obligation: Every callback path rejects direct calls and mismatched loan parameters.

vectors.title: First-depositor or donation share inflation
vectors.description: Shares are minted as assets * totalSupply / totalAssets with no virtual offset and no dead shares. An empty vault can be inflated by a donation.
vectors.exploit: Deposit 1 wei, donate a large amount directly to the vault, then watch a subsequent depositor mint 0 shares while their assets stay in the vault.
vectors.remediation: Use virtual shares and virtual assets, burn a permanent minimum liquidity, or require a non-zero first deposit that cannot be fully withdrawn.
vectors.proof_obligation: Model empty-vault, donation, and rounding-down-to-zero states and prove shares cannot be cheaply inflated.

vectors.title: Division before multiplication or attacker-favorable rounding
vectors.description: Share, fee, or exchange-rate math divides before it multiplies, or always rounds in the depositor or borrower's favor.
vectors.exploit: Repeat tiny deposits, withdrawals, or swaps so truncation accumulates into extractable value, or empty a pool via repeated 1-wei operations.
vectors.remediation: Multiply first, use mulDiv with explicit rounding direction, and round against the user on mint and in favor of the protocol on burn.
vectors.proof_obligation: Differential-test every value-bearing formula against a full-precision reference over boundary inputs.
real_incidents: Multiple vault and AMM rounding findings

vectors.title: Privileged state change without authorization
vectors.description: A function that mints, sets an owner, upgrades, withdraws reserves, or changes a critical parameter is callable by anyone.
vectors.exploit: Call the function from an arbitrary account and seize funds, roles, or upgrade rights.
vectors.remediation: Gate the function with a role check bound to msg.sender (or a validated signature), not tx.origin.
vectors.proof_obligation: Enumerate intended callers and prove every privileged write is unreachable otherwise.

vectors.title: Authorization via tx.origin
vectors.description: Privilege is granted when tx.origin matches an owner, so any contract the owner interacts with can impersonate them.
vectors.exploit: Phish the owner into calling an attacker contract that then calls the privileged function.
vectors.remediation: Authorize with msg.sender or an EIP-712 signature bound to nonce, chain, and contract.
vectors.proof_obligation: No authorization predicate reads tx.origin.

vectors.title: Signature missing nonce, chain, or domain binding
vectors.description: Signed authorizations do not bind nonce, chain id, verifying contract, and action, or ecrecover's zero address is accepted.
vectors.exploit: Replay a valid signature on another chain, contract, or after a state change, or submit a malleable s-value.
vectors.remediation: Use EIP-712 with name, version, chainId, verifyingContract, a monotonic nonce, and reject ecrecover == address(0).
vectors.proof_obligation: Replay across nonce, chain, contract, parameter, and deadline boundaries fails.

vectors.title: Unprotected initializer or implementation takeover
vectors.description: A proxy implementation can be initialized by anyone, or the implementation contract itself is left uninitialized so an attacker becomes owner and selfdestructs it.
vectors.exploit: Front-run initialize on the proxy, or take over the implementation, destroy it, and brick every proxy pointing at it.
vectors.remediation: Disable initializers in the implementation constructor and restrict initialize to the deployment transaction.
vectors.proof_obligation: Race initialization and repeated initialization on both proxy and implementation fail.

vectors.title: Proxy storage layout collision across upgrades
vectors.description: An upgrade inserts a state variable without a storage gap, shifting later slots and corrupting balances or owners.
vectors.exploit: After the upgrade, existing storage is interpreted as a different type or owner, enabling unauthorized withdrawals.
vectors.remediation: Append-only storage, reserved __gap slots, and ERC-7201 namespaced storage.
vectors.proof_obligation: Storage-layout diffs across every upgrade path show no slot reuse.

vectors.title: Value-changing swap or liquidity op without slippage bound
vectors.description: A swap, zap, or liquidity change does not enforce a caller-supplied minOut/maxIn and deadline.
vectors.exploit: Sandwich the transaction: move price against the user, let the trade execute at a worse rate, then restore price and extract the difference.
vectors.remediation: Require minAmountOut or maxAmountIn and a deadline on every value-changing AMM operation.
vectors.proof_obligation: Moving price before execution reverts outside the user's tolerance.

vectors.title: Flash-loaned voting power or same-block execution
vectors.description: Voting power is read from the live token balance and proposals can be executed in the same window they are passed.
vectors.exploit: Borrow governance tokens, pass and execute a malicious proposal, return the tokens.
vectors.remediation: Checkpoint votes, use a past block for snapshots, and enforce a timelock before execution.
vectors.proof_obligation: Temporary token balances cannot change the outcome of a proposal that can be executed.

vectors.title: Cross-chain message replay or unverified root
vectors.description: A destination-chain executor does not consume a message id, or accepts a zero/stale merkle root, or does not bind source and destination domain.
vectors.exploit: Replay a valid lock/burn proof, or submit a proof against an uninitialized root, and mint unbacked tokens.
vectors.remediation: Bind source chain, dest chain, nonce, recipient, and amount; consume the message id exactly once; reject zero roots.
vectors.proof_obligation: The same valid message cannot credit value twice and a zero root cannot authorize anything.

vectors.title: Unprotected selfdestruct or force-send assumption
vectors.description: Anyone can destroy the contract, or logic assumes address(this).balance is only increased by intended deposits (broken by selfdestruct / beacon force-send).
vectors.exploit: Destroy the contract and take its funds, or inflate a balance-based accounting assumption.
vectors.remediation: Remove selfdestruct on post-Cancun chains or gate it strictly; never treat raw ETH balance as an invariant.
vectors.proof_obligation: Unauthorized accounts cannot reach destruction, and accounting uses tracked deposits not raw balance.

vectors.title: Solana/Anchor missing signer or arbitrary CPI
vectors.description: A privileged Anchor account is not Signer, or a CPI target program is not constrained, or ownership is not checked.
vectors.exploit: Pass an attacker-controlled account or program and steal tokens or rewrite state.
vectors.remediation: Use Signer, Account<'info, T> with owner and has_one constraints, and bind CPI program ids.
vectors.proof_obligation: Every privileged account must be a signer or PDA with canonical bump; every CPI program is allowlisted.

vectors.title: Duplicate mutable accounts or spoofable sysvar
vectors.description: Two mutable role accounts can be the same key, or Clock/Rent/token program identity is not typed.
vectors.exploit: Pass the same account for vault and attacker, or substitute Token-2022 / a fake Clock to bypass checks.
vectors.remediation: Require key inequality, typed Sysvar accounts, and explicit token program identity.
vectors.proof_obligation: Same-account pairs and spoofed sysvars/token programs are rejected.

vectors.title: Move missing signer or capability check
vectors.description: An entry function mutates a global resource without requiring the intended signer or capability.
vectors.exploit: Call the entry function from an unrelated signer and take or corrupt the resource.
vectors.remediation: Require signer, store capabilities under the rightful address, and abort on wrong-address borrows.
vectors.proof_obligation: Every global write is gated by signer or capability ownership.

vectors.title: Vyper compiler version with known reentrancy or storage bugs
vectors.description: The pinned Vyper version is in a range with a public compiler bug (reentrancy lock 0.2.15–0.3.0, storage corruption 0.3.7).
vectors.exploit: Use the compiler bug rather than a source-level mistake — the @nonreentrant decorator or storage layout does not behave as written.
vectors.remediation: Recompile with a maintained Vyper release and rerun invariant tests.
vectors.proof_obligation: The deployed compiler version is not in any published affected range.

vectors.title: Unbounded loop over a user-growable array
vectors.description: A public function iterates an array that any user can grow, so the call can exceed the block gas limit and lock funds.
vectors.exploit: Push enough entries that distribute/withdraw can never succeed.
vectors.remediation: Paginate, use pull-over-push, or cap the collection independently of users.
vectors.proof_obligation: The loop bound is independent of unbounded user input.

vectors.title: Validator-predictable randomness
vectors.description: A lottery, NFT rarity, or keeper election uses block attributes an proposer can bias.
vectors.exploit: Search feasible timestamps or prevrandao values and only publish a block (or submit a tx) when the outcome is favorable.
vectors.remediation: Use a VRF or a commit-reveal bound to msg.sender.
vectors.proof_obligation: Outcomes cannot be predicted or biased by proposers or submitters.

vectors.title: Fee-on-transfer or rebasing token mis-accounting
vectors.description: The protocol credits the requested amount rather than the actual balance delta, so fee-on-transfer or rebasing tokens desynchronize shares.
vectors.exploit: Deposit a FoT token; the vault owes more shares than assets received. Later withdraw more than the pool holds.
vectors.remediation: Measure balance before and after every transfer and account the delta.
vectors.proof_obligation: FoT and rebasing fixtures cannot inflate shares or steal value.

vectors.title: CREATE2 metamorphic implementation swap
vectors.description: A CREATE2 address is trusted after first deployment; an operator can selfdestruct and redeploy different bytecode at the same address.
vectors.exploit: Deploy honest code, pass a review, destroy, redeploy a drain at the same address.
vectors.remediation: Hash-pin runtime bytecode, avoid selfdestruct, or treat CREATE2 identities as mutable.
vectors.proof_obligation: The codehash at each trusted CREATE2 address cannot change after first use.
real_incidents: Metamorphic contract research / several rug classes

vectors.title: L2 sequencer downtime or stale oracle on rollup
vectors.description: An L2 protocol reads a price feed without checking the sequencer uptime feed or a heartbeat, so prices freeze during an outage.
vectors.exploit: After a sequencer outage, liquidate or borrow against a stale price before the feed catches up.
vectors.remediation: Check the L2 sequencer uptime feed, enforce heartbeat, and pause risky operations when stale.
vectors.proof_obligation: Stale, incomplete, and post-outage rounds cannot authorize borrow or liquidation.

vectors.title: Self-liquidation or bad-debt socialization hole
vectors.description: A borrower can capture their own liquidation bonus, or insolvency is not recognized so healthy users become trapped.
vectors.exploit: Flash-crash a price, liquidate yourself for the incentive, or leave bad debt that bricks withdrawals.
vectors.remediation: Forbid self-liquidation, accrue before seize, and define a bad-debt socialization path.
vectors.proof_obligation: Self, aliased, and undercollateralized paths cannot extract a bonus or trap solvent users.

vectors.title: Huff stack underflow or payable fallthrough
vectors.description: A Huff macro does not guarantee stack height, or a dispatcher falls through to privileged logic on short calldata or nonzero value.
vectors.exploit: Send crafted calldata or value to underflow the stack or reach an admin path.
vectors.remediation: Trace stack height on every branch; reject short calldata and unexpected CALLVALUE.
vectors.proof_obligation: Every macro branch has enough operands and every selector rejects unintended value and length.

vectors.title: Cairo/Starknet caller authorization gap
vectors.description: A Cairo external function writes storage without comparing get_caller_address to an owner or role.
vectors.exploit: Invoke the external entry point from an arbitrary account.
vectors.remediation: Assert caller against the stored owner or a component AccessControl role.
vectors.proof_obligation: Every storage-writing external function authenticates the caller.

vectors.title: Sway/Fuel msg_sender authorization gap
vectors.description: A storage(write) ABI method does not require msg_sender to match the owner.
vectors.exploit: Call the ABI method from an unauthorized identity.
vectors.remediation: Require msg_sender().unwrap() == storage.owner.read().
vectors.proof_obligation: Every write method authenticates the caller.

vectors.title: Tact/TON receiver without sender check
vectors.description: A Tact receiver mutates owner-controlled state without comparing sender() to the owner.
vectors.exploit: Send the message from an arbitrary TON account.
vectors.remediation: Require sender() == self.owner before privileged mutations.
vectors.proof_obligation: Every privileged receiver authenticates sender().

vectors.title: Donation or reserve path skips the solvency check
vectors.description: A donate/reserve function reduces collateral or equity without running the same account-health check as withdraw, borrow, or liquidate.
vectors.exploit: Flash-loan, loop leverage, donate collateral to reserves while debt stays, then self-liquidate at a discount and repay the loan.
vectors.remediation: Call the canonical health/liquidity check on every path that reduces collateral, including donations and reserve transfers. Treat donate as a withdraw.
vectors.proof_obligation: Every balance-reducing entry, including donate, reverts when it would leave the account under the liquidation threshold.

vectors.title: Permissionless market or strategy registration treated as trusted
vectors.description: Anyone can register a market, pool, or strategy that later supplies prices, rewards, or callbacks. The protocol treats that address as honest.
vectors.exploit: Register a fake SY/market, re-enter harvest, inflate a balance-delta reward, and drain real assets attributed to the fake market.
vectors.remediation: Allowlist markets, require a timelocked governance add, and never measure rewards as an untrusted balance delta.
vectors.proof_obligation: An arbitrary contract cannot become a reward or price source without a privileged, delayed listing.

vectors.title: Flash-loan, hook, or zap callback accepts attacker parameters
vectors.description: A callback meant for a pool, lender, or hook does not bind caller, initiator, and the encoded action, so it can be invoked as a confused deputy.
vectors.exploit: Call the callback directly with another user's position parameters (or a crafted hook) and steal collateral that the user approved to the zap.
vectors.remediation: Require msg.sender to be the canonical pool, bind initiator, hash the intended action, and never trust leftover approvals on helper contracts.
vectors.proof_obligation: Direct calls and substituted parameters revert; standing zap approvals cannot close or reopen a third-party position.

vectors.title: Concentrated-liquidity tick-boundary double count
vectors.description: When sqrtP sits exactly on a tick, liquidity is added both to the in-range accumulator and again when the tick is crossed.
vectors.exploit: Flash-loan a multi-tick swap that parks price on a boundary, mint, cross, and withdraw the double-counted liquidity.
vectors.remediation: Treat equality of sqrtP and nextSqrtP as a first-class case. Fuzz tick-boundary crossings and exact-tick mints.
vectors.proof_obligation: Mint + cross at an exact tick never increases active liquidity by more than the minted amount.

vectors.title: Liquid-staking exchange rate used as a spot oracle
vectors.description: Collateral or mint logic prices an LST/LRT from a same-block share/asset rate or a thin wrapper, which a donation or rebase can move.
vectors.exploit: Donate into the rate source or use a wrapper with manipulable totalAssets, borrow against the inflated LST, restore.
vectors.remediation: Use an independent oracle with a freshness bound, or a liquidity-weighted TWAP, never a raw exchangeRate() as USD.
vectors.proof_obligation: A same-transaction donation or rebase cannot increase borrow power.

vectors.title: Uniswap v4 / hook callback trust
vectors.description: A v4-style hook or unlock callback mutates balances or prices and is reachable from an untrusted pool or during a transient unlock.
vectors.exploit: Attach a malicious hook, or re-enter through unlockCallback, and observe or steal reserves mid-swap.
vectors.remediation: Authenticate the pool, keep hooks CEI-safe, and treat unlock as a reentrancy window.
vectors.proof_obligation: Hook and unlock paths cannot be invoked by an arbitrary caller and cannot observe inconsistent reserves.

vectors.title: Permit2 / allowance-transfer signature or witness gap
vectors.description: A Permit2 integration does not bind witness, nonce, spender, or deadline, or a helper keeps a standing Permit2 allowance.
vectors.exploit: Replay a permit, substitute witness data, or drain via a leftover Permit2 allowance after a zap.
vectors.remediation: Bind witness in the typed hash, expire allowances, and never leave infinite Permit2 approvals on helpers.
vectors.proof_obligation: Replayed or witness-substituted permits revert; helper allowances are zero after use.

vectors.title: Async vault request/claim accounting desync
vectors.description: An ERC-7540-style async vault prices a claim against a later share rate, or lets a controller steal a pending request.
vectors.exploit: Request at one rate, inflate or crash totalAssets before claim, or take over controller and claim someone else's request.
vectors.remediation: Snapshot the rate at request time or bound slippage on claim; bind controller and owner; lock pending assets.
vectors.proof_obligation: A pending request cannot be claimed by a stranger or at an attacker-moved rate outside the user's bound.

vectors.title: ERC-4337 validateUserOp reads mutable third-party state
vectors.description: Account or paymaster validation makes external calls or reads storage an adversary can change between simulation and execution.
vectors.exploit: Grief the bundler (validation passes, execution reverts) or drain a paymaster that trusted a mutable allowance.
vectors.remediation: Keep validateUserOp free of untrusted external calls; bound paymaster gas; do not read third-party allowances.
vectors.proof_obligation: Validation is a function of the userOp, the account's own storage, and block values the ERC allows.

vectors.title: Rewards measured as an untrusted balance delta
vectors.description: A harvest computes rewards as token.balanceOf(this) after an external redeem minus the snapshot before. A re-entering or fake market can deposit during the call.
vectors.exploit: Re-enter harvest (or register a fake market that deposits during redeemRewards) so the delta is attacker capital, minted as shares, then withdrawn.
vectors.remediation: Use explicit reward amounts from a trusted interface, take a reentrancy lock, and never treat a balance delta from an untrusted callee as income.
vectors.proof_obligation: A re-entrant deposit or fake market cannot increase credited rewards.
